titulo: Adult attachment styles and psychological birth trauma symptoms: A cross-sectional survey of postpartum women in Australia
resumo: Background Psychological birth trauma (PBT) has been proposed as a broader construct encompassing childbirth-related psychological distress, including but not limited to symptoms consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder. Attachment theory suggests that adult attachment dimensions are associated with differences in threat appraisal, affect regulation, and help-seeking; however, their relationship with childbirth-related trauma symptoms and birth satisfaction remains unclear. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 940 postpartum women in Australia (≤24 months postpartum) who had experienced an early-term or full-term (≥37 weeks), vaginal, singleton birth and whose infant did not require neonatal intensive care or special care. Participants completed a demographic questionnaire, the Adult Attachment Questionnaire, City Birth Trauma Scale, and Australian Birth Satisfaction Scale-Revised. Data were analysed in SPSS, with measures scored according to published procedures. Adult attachment anxiety and avoidance were examined as continuous dimensions as the primary analytic approach and via median-split quadrants to derive attachment classifications for secondary analyses. Childbirth-related trauma symptoms were analysed dimensionally, and probable PTSD was identified using a published algorithm. Birth satisfaction was analysed as a continuous outcome. Results In the primary dimensional analyses, higher attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance were each associated with greater childbirth-related trauma symptom severity and lower birth satisfaction. In secondary exploratory quadrant-based analyses, women with secure attachment classifications reported the lowest trauma symptoms and most favourable birth appraisals, whereas those with attachments classified as disorganised/unresolved reported the highest symptom burden and the least favourable appraisals of stress, self-related attributes, and quality of care. Overall, 14.8% of participants met the published threshold for probable childbirth-related PTSD, with the lowest proportion observed in the secure group and the highest in the disorganised/unresolved group, based on the exploratory quadrant-derived classifications. Discussion Higher attachment anxiety and avoidance were associated with elevated childbirth-related trauma symptoms and poorer childbirth appraisals within the current sample. Secondary exploratory attachment classification analyses further demonstrated broadly consistent patterns. These findings highlight the potential value of further investigating attachment-informed and trauma-informed approaches within relational maternity care, continuity models of midwifery care, and postnatal psychological support.

titulo: Gene-based association analysis of depression risk among European ancestry Parkinson’s disease patients
resumo: Depression is one of the most common and disabling non-motor symptoms in Parkinson’s disease (PD), yet its genetic basis remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the genetic contributions to depression in PD by estimating the burden from common as well as low-frequency single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) within genes previously implicated in PD or depression risk among European ancestry PD patients from three population-based studies. Using gene-based association analyses (SKAT, Burden, and SKAT-O) in the PASIDA, PEG, and PPMI studies, we evaluated SNP sets in gene regions previously linked to PD or depression. Among PD-related genes, meta-analysis identified a significant association between KRTCAP2 and self-reported depression diagnosis in PD (SKAT-O p = 4.33 × 10⁻⁵), which remained significant after false discovery rate correction. A higher genetic burden in KRTCAP2 was associated with 20% increased odds of depression (OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.04–1.38). TRAF5 and LRRK2 showed marginal associations. Among depression-related genes, SPPL3 and ERBB4 were associated with depression diagnosis history, and FNIP2 was associated with current depressive symptoms. The PD polygenic risk score was not associated with depression in PD, while a higher depression polygenic risk score was significantly associated with increased odds of depression diagnosis in both cohorts and the meta-analysis (OR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.13–1.40). Our findings highlight immune-related genes such as KRTCAP2 and TRAF5 as potential contributors to depression in PD. Additionally, the depression PRS shows statistically significant association with depression diagnosis in PD, suggesting that a general depression-related genetic liability contributes to this non-motor feature in PD. Together, these results suggest that depression in PD may involve both shared and disease-specific genetic mechanisms, offering new insights into its pathogenesis and potential therapeutic targets.

titulo: Artificial intelligence literacy, artificial intelligence anxiety, and career optimism among university music students: a cross-sectional study
resumo: Objective To examine the levels of artificial intelligence (AI) literacy, AI anxiety, and career optimism among university music students, their associations, and the independent associations of AI literacy and AI anxiety with career optimism after adjustment for relevant background factors. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted from May to July 2026 among students from five undergraduate music institutions in eastern China using convenience sampling. A total of 453 valid questionnaires were included in the analysis. Participants completed the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale for Chinese College Students (AILS-CCS), the Chinese version of the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale (AIAS), and the Career Optimism Subscale (COS). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t tests , one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation analysis, and hierarchical multiple linear regression. Results Mean scores for AI literacy, AI anxiety, and career optimism were 52.97 ± 10.05, 83.85 ± 22.96, and 37.87 ± 8.02, respectively. Students with prior AI training and those reporting more frequent AI use showed higher AI literacy and career optimism and lower AI anxiety. AI literacy was positively associated with career optimism (r = 0.444, p < 0.001), whereas AI anxiety was negatively associated with career optimism (r = −0.461, p < 0.001). After adjustment for gender, year of study, music specialization, prior AI training, and frequency of AI use, AI literacy remained positively associated with career optimism (β = 0.314, p < 0.001), whereas AI anxiety remained negatively associated with career optimism (β = −0.326, p < 0.001). The final model explained 33.0% of the variance in career optimism. Conclusion AI literacy and AI anxiety were independently associated with career optimism among university music students. These findings suggest that students' perceptions of AI-related competence and technological concerns are relevant to their career expectations. Music institutions may consider AI education that combines practical competence with critical understanding of AI's implications for artistic identity, professional value, and future career development. Future longitudinal research is needed to clarify the temporal relationships among AI literacy, AI anxiety, and career optimism.

titulo: Barriers and enablers shaping autistic college students’ pathways into advanced manufacturing careers
resumo: Objective Autistic college students are strongly represented in STEM disciplines, yet continue to experience disproportionately poor employment outcomes after graduation. This study explores their lived experiences navigating educational and career pathways into advanced manufacturing, a high-demand sector facing persistent workforce shortages and substantial public investment, yet largely absent from autism and employment scholarship to date. Method Sixteen autistic STEM undergraduates (current or previous) from across the US participated in three 90-minute focus groups conducted via Zoom. Sessions examined students' career aspirations, job search experiences, perceived barriers, and support needs, and were analysed using thematic analysis to identify enablers and systemic barriers shaping participants' transitions from education to industry. Results Participants demonstrated proactive engagement in developing technical skills through coursework, self-directed learning, and hands-on experiences. However, they encountered opaque hiring processes, unclear interview expectations, limited access to prior industry experience, workplace sensory challenges, and fragmented institutional support, often relying on informal networks and AI-based tools to compensate. Participants emphasized inclusive, sensory-aware learning environments, structured career preparation, and autism-informed mentorship as critical bridges between academic training and workforce expectations. Conclusions Employment disparities reflect systemic misalignment rather than individual deficits, underscoring the need to redesign education-to-work pathways that recognize and leverage autistic strengths.

titulo: Mental health symptoms and everyday social interaction among university students: an exploratory intensive longitudinal study of relational events within bounded peer networks
resumo: Background Mental health symptoms are closely linked to social relationships, yet most research examines social connectedness through stable ties or retrospective reports. Less is known about how symptoms are associated with the unfolding micro-dynamics of everyday interaction. This exploratory study examined whether depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and ADHD symptoms were differentially associated with face-to-face contact and received emotional support among university students. Methods Data came from the PeerSmart Network Study, an intensive longitudinal social network study combining smartphone-based ecological momentary assessment with roster-based sociometric measurement. Thirty-eight students from two bounded academic cohorts completed baseline mental health measures and participated in a seven-day assessment period with three prompts per day, contributing 657 short surveys. At each prompt, participants reported face-to-face contacts lasting at least five minutes and received emotional support since the previous survey. Given the intensive but small-scale design, the analyses were intended to model micro-level interaction processes within bounded peer contexts rather than to estimate population-level associations. Dynamic Network Actor Models were estimated separately for the bachelor and master cohorts. Received emotional support was modelled as a directed event process, whereas face-to-face contact was modelled as an undirected coordination process. Results Mental health symptom levels were more consistently associated with received emotional support than with general face-to-face contact. Anxiety symptoms showed a positive association with receiving emotional support in both cohorts. Depressive symptoms were negatively associated with receiving emotional support in the bachelor cohort, and ADHD symptoms were negatively associated with receiving support in both cohorts. In contrast, face-to-face contact showed little evidence of overall involvement differences by symptom level, suggesting that general social exposure was more strongly associated with prior interaction history and opportunity structures. Conclusions The findings provide preliminary evidence that mental health symptoms are not uniformly associated with everyday social interaction. Rather, symptom levels appeared to be most relevant for emotionally meaningful support exchanges. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing general social contact from support-related interaction and suggest that student mental health interventions should attend not only to social connectedness, but also to the concrete contexts in which support is mobilized or missed.

titulo: Irritability in Adult Depression and Anxiety: A Clinically Useful Signal Amid an Imprecise Construct
resumo: A brief consideration of the conceptual and diagnostic tidiness of irritability associated with depression and anxiety in adults. Despite evidence for its conceptual untidiness, there are practical issues that the clinician may consider when diagnosing and treating depression or anxiety.

titulo: Commentary: A Neurodiversity-Affirming Framework for Evaluating Autism Support Research
resumo: Despite growing interest in neurodiversity-affirming research, many studies examining interventions, practices, or services designed to support autistic individuals in daily life and well-being still prioritise reducing autistic traits over well-being and autonomy. However, there are currently no universally accepted definitions or frameworks for appraising the extent to which specific support programmes align with neurodiversity-affirming principles. This commentary introduces a five-principle framework developed through systematic appraisal of the literature and collaboration with autistic, clinical and academic contributors. The framework assesses the following aspects of autism support studies: (a) strengths-based focus, (b) support for self-determination and autonomy, (c) adaptation of the environment and upskilling others, (d) diverse communication methods and (e) respect for sensory and processing differences. This preliminary framework may offer a transparent method for evaluating alignment with principles drawn from neurodiversity scholarship and social/interactional models of disability and guiding ethical, inclusive practice. Potential applications include its use in reviews or training to support research and practice that centre autistic quality of life. Lay Abstract Many autism studies focus on changing autistic behaviours. However, autistic people and researchers have increasingly called for approaches that support well-being, quality of life and acceptance of autistic differences. Currently, there is no clear way to assess whether autism research follows these ideas. This commentary presents a framework for evaluating autism support research. The framework examines whether studies focus on strengths, support independence and choice, adapt environments to meet people’s needs, recognise different ways of communicating and respect sensory differences. The framework was developed using existing research and feedback from autistic people, clinicians and researchers. It can help researchers identify studies that align with neurodiversity-affirming values and encourage more supportive and inclusive autism research in the future.

titulo: Characterizing Autism Phenotype Onset in the Electronic Health Records to Enable Age‐Specific Screening
resumo: Autism exhibits substantial phenotypic heterogeneity, yet age‐dependent variation in phenotypic profiles and onset timing remains poorly understood. We aimed to characterize stage‐specific phenotypes and temporal onset patterns of autism using longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs). We analyzed EHR data from Columbia University Irving Medical Center. Autism cases were stratified by age at diagnosis. Phenotype enrichment analyses were performed using chi‐square and Fisher's exact tests to identify phenotypes overrepresented in autism cases compared with matched controls, and temporal patterns of phenotype onset were subsequently evaluated to identify stage‐specific clinical signatures and provide insight into differences between early‐ and late‐diagnosed individuals. Among 4818 cases and 1433 phenotypes, 195 and 155 were enriched in toddlerhood and adolescence groups. Early diagnosed individuals exhibited a higher prevalence of sensory‐related conditions, greater exposure to maternal and perinatal complications than their matched controls (all ORs > 1; p < 0.01), and earlier onset of neurologic features, including coordination abnormalities and convulsions, compared with later‐diagnosed individuals. The study provides a publicly accessible resource to enrich autism‐related phenotypic profiles, uncovering notable phenotypic differences and variations in timing of phenotype onset between early‐diagnosed and later‐diagnosed individuals. These findings underscore phenotypic heterogeneity and highlight the need for age‐sensitive screening strategies. To our knowledge, this is among the first studies to jointly characterize phenotypic profiles and their temporal onset patterns across developmental stages in autism using longitudinal EHR data. These findings offer novel insights into age‐dependent clinical signatures, informing earlier and more precise screening strategies.

titulo: Multiple discrimination at work and depressive symptoms in young adults
resumo: Background We aimed to estimate the implications of cumulative exposure to discrimination at work for mental health among young adults. Our specific objective was to investigate if experiencing multiple types of discrimination at work is associated with depressive symptoms. Methods We analyzed cross-sectional questionnaire data from 1066 participants (56.8% female, mean age 31.3 years) of the third phase of the German Study on Occupational Allergy Risks (2017–2018, response 47.3%). Participants were asked whether during the last twelve months they had experienced one or more of seven types of discrimination at their workplace. The Patient Health Questionnaire-2 (PHQ-2) was used for screening of symptoms of depression. We performed multivariate logistic regression to estimate the association between the number of experienced types of discrimination at work and depressive symptoms. Results Discrimination due to sex was the most often reported type (6.1% of participants). Experience of two or more forms of discrimination was indicated by 2.5% of the participants. One hundred four individuals (9.8%) were screened positive for depression. Before adjustment for work stress, individuals reporting two or more types of discrimination at work had more than six times the odds of depressive symptoms compared to the non-exposed reference group (Odds Ratio (OR): 6.31, 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 2.67 to 14.89). After adjustment for work stress, the OR for the association between two or more types of discrimination and depressive symptoms was 3.92 (95% CI: 1.40 to 11.01). Conclusion Our results support the hypothesis of an association between exposure to multiple discrimination at work and poor mental health, even though our effect estimates suffer from low statistical precision. Furthermore, the design of our analysis does not permit causal statements. In view of the entire scientific body of studies in the field, we argue that measures to reduce or abolish discrimination may be seen as important means of protecting mental health and well-being.

titulo: Considering Autism in Binge-Type Eating Disorders: Broadening Beyond an Anorexia Nervosa-Focused Model
resumo: Purpose of Review Research on Autism in eating disorders (EDs) has historically focused on anorexia nervosa (AN), with comparatively limited attention given to binge-type EDs such as bulimia nervosa (BN) and binge eating disorder (BED). This review summarises emerging evidence on Autism in binge-type EDs and highlights key clinical and research implications. Recent Findings Emerging evidence suggests that Autism is over-represented in BN and BED, although prevalence appears lower than in AN and research remains methodologically limited. Recent studies suggest that affective and reward-related processes, alongside sensory differences, may contribute to binge-type presentations. Co-occurring ADHD appears particularly relevant and may complicate recognition, clinical presentation, and treatment. Autism also remains under-recognised in binge-type EDs by ED services, where existing adaptations remain largely derived from AN models. Summary Current AN-centric models may inadequately capture Neurodivergence in binge-type EDs. More transdiagnostic, mechanism-informed research and treatment approaches are needed.

titulo: Intervenções da terapia cognitiva-comportamental para o luto por suicídio: uma revisão de escopo
resumo: Suicide bereavement may involve different psychological consequences and require interventions tailored to bereaved individuals’ needs. This study aimed to analyze cognitive-behavioral therapy-based interventions investigated among people bereaved by suicide. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute recommendations and reported according to PRISMA-ScR. Searches were performed in six databases and updated in August 2026. Nine publications, corresponding to five primary empirical investigations, were included, all conducted in European countries. The interventions were heterogeneous regarding duration, delivery modality, therapeutic components, sample characteristics, and outcomes. Advances were identified in the use of structured interventions, online delivery, different therapeutic targets, and the investigation of variables associated with therapeutic processes. However, clinical outcomes were not consistent across investigations. Available evidence does not support prioritizing a specific protocol, therapeutic component, duration, or delivery modality. The findings indicate a developing field and highlight the need to expand and diversify its evidence base.

titulo: Childhood Adversity and Anxiety, Depression, and Suicidal Behaviors Among African‐Origin Emerging Adults in the United States: Findings From an Online Panel
resumo: This study examined associations between adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and anxiety symptoms, depressive symptoms, lifetime suicidal ideation, and lifetime suicide attempt among African‐origin emerging adults in the United States. Data were drawn from a cross‐sectional, nonprobability online panel of 537 participants aged 18–29, comprising foreign‐born first‐generation African immigrants and U.S.‐born second‐generation participants with African‐born parents. We assessed ACEs using an expanded cumulative index that included conventional household adversities and four community‐level adversities. We used separate multivariable linear and logistic regression models to examine associations between ACEs and each mental health outcome. We also ran generation‐stratified models and formal tests of ACEs × generation interactions. Higher ACE scores were associated with greater anxiety, depressive symptom severity, and higher odds of lifetime suicidal ideation and lifetime suicide attempt. Associations were statistically significant within both generational groups. Generation significantly moderated the associations between ACEs and suicidal ideation and suicide attempt, with stronger associations among first‐generation participants. Generation did not significantly moderate the associations of ACEs with anxiety or depression. Second‐generation participants had higher overall odds of suicidal ideation than first‐generation participants. ACEs were consistently associated with adverse mental health outcomes among African‐origin emerging adults in this U.S.‐based online panel. The findings support culturally responsive, trauma‐informed assessment and intervention while underscoring the need for longitudinal research examining how developmental, migration‐related, and sociocultural contexts may contribute to these associations.

titulo: Associations among perceived negative consequences, perceived deterioration in well-being, fear of progression, and probable depression in Chinese adults with chronic kidney disease: a cross-sectional path analysis
resumo: Introduction Individuals with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are vulnerable to probable depression. Perceived negative consequences (PNC) of CKD, perceived deterioration in well-being (PDW), and fear of progression (FoP) are commonly experienced in this population. This cross-sectional study examined the associations among PNC, PDW, FoP, and probable depression. It also tested the indirect associations of PNC and PDW with probable depression through FoP. Additionally, gender differences in these direct and indirect pathways were explored. Methods In this cross-sectional study, a total of 456 Chinese CKD patients were recruited using convenience sampling. Participants completed standardized self-report questionnaires at a single time point. Path analysis and multi-group analysis by gender were conducted using Mplus 8.3. Results The prevalence of probable depression was 37.3%. PDW, PNC, and FoP were positively and significantly associated with probable depression. Significant indirect associations of both PDW and PNC with probable depression through FoP were observed. Significant gender differences were found in the PDW → FoP, PNC → FoP, and PDW → probable depression associations, as well as in the indirect associations of both PDW and PNC with probable depression through FoP. All these associations were stronger among females than males. No significant gender differences were observed in the FoP → probable depression or PNC → probable depression associations. Conclusion Higher levels of PNC, PDW, and FoP were associated with a greater likelihood of probable depression among individuals with CKD. The significant indirect associations through FoP were consistent with its potential explanatory role in the proposed model. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine whether addressing illness appraisals or FoP can improve psychological well-being in this population.

titulo: When doctors falter: Resilience in modern obstetrics and gynecology, a narrative review
resumo: The practice of obstetrics and gynecology (O&G) is frequently regarded as one of the most demanding medical specialties, with physicians being called to duty at any hour of the day or night, with acute patient demands requiring prompt management. Consequently, high levels of physician burnout and psychological distress have been reported among O&G healthcare professionals, with these challenges further compounded by the COVID‐19 pandemic. Despite the prevalence of mental health difficulties, many healthcare professionals do not seek out professional intervention and support. Within O&G, trainees appear vulnerable, with studies reporting significant rates of stress, anxiety, depression, and burnout. These mental health challenges contribute to reduced job satisfaction, increased intentions to leave specialist training programs, and growing concerns regarding physician attrition and workforce retention. In this context, physician resilience (i.e., the ability to excel in the face of adversity) emerges as an area worthy of exploration. This narrative review explores the multifaceted emotional and practical elements of physician resilience and grit in contemporary obstetrics and gynecology practice. A comprehensive literature search was conducted using PubMed and the Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland library database, employing terms related to physician wellbeing, burnout and interventions specifically related to obstetrics and gynecology. Inclusion criteria were limited to full text, English‐language articles published within the past 10 years to ensure relevance to contemporary practice. The review examines the interrelationship between physician burnout, mental health challenges among O&G trainees, and their impact on attrition rates. We aim to highlight the need for practical interventions at institutional levels with consideration of environmental/workplace factors, which might improve physician wellbeing and grit, strengthen workforce retention, and ultimately optimize patient care.

titulo: Academic procrastination and test anxiety as predictors of perceived academic performance in Peruvian university students
resumo: Academic procrastination and test anxiety are common phenomena in university life, capable of affecting students' perceptions of their own academic performance. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 323 Peruvian university students from various majors, selected by convenience sampling. Validated questionnaires were used to measure academic procrastination, test anxiety, and perceived academic performance. The results indicate that higher levels of test anxiety (β = -0.262) and academic procrastination (β = -0.600) reduce students' self-perception of their academic performance, together explaining 47.9% of the variance (adjusted R 2 = 0.479). Gender differences were also identified: women reported significantly higher levels of test anxiety, while men showed higher levels of academic procrastination. These findings reveal gender-based patterns and confirm that both anxiety and procrastination have a negative impact on self-perception of academic performance, highlighting the need for intervention strategies focused on emotional management and the strengthening of study habits.

titulo: Latent profiles of Big Five personality traits among Chinese university students and their associations with psychological distress and health-related quality of life: The moderating role of the school sports environment
resumo: Variable-centred research overlooks how personality dimensions combine within individuals. This study used latent profile analysis (LPA) to identify Big Five personality profiles among 2291 Chinese university students, examine profile differences in depression, anxiety, stress, and mental and physical health-related quality of life, and test whether the school sports environment moderated profile differences in health-related quality of life. Participants completed the Big Five Inventory-10 (BFI-10), the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (DASS-21), the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36), and a 47-item School Sports Environment Questionnaire. A three-profile solution was retained, comprising Average (68.4%), Emotionally Fragile (6.3%; low extraversion, low conscientiousness, high neuroticism), and Resilient (25.3%; high extraversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness, openness, low neuroticism). The Resilient profile exhibited higher mental and physical health-related quality-of-life scores and lower levels of depression, anxiety, and stress, whereas the Emotionally Fragile profile showed the opposite pattern; all pairwise differences were significant (adjusted p < 0.001). A more supportive school sports environment was associated with higher mental and physical health-related quality-of-life scores across profiles. The Profile × School Sports Environment interaction was significant for both mental health-related quality of life, F(2, 2280) = 7.07, p < 0.001, and physical health-related quality of life, F(2, 2280) = 4.70, p = 0.009. Simple slope analyses indicated significant positive associations in all three profiles, with the strongest associations observed in the Emotionally Fragile profile. These findings extend person-centred evidence on personality and health among Chinese university students and identify profile-dependent associations with the school sports environment.

titulo: A massively parallel reporter assay of MECP2 cis-regulatory elements reveals genetic candidates for male-biased autism
periodico: The American Journal of Human Genetics
resumo: Autism affects male individuals four times more often than female individuals, yet the basis of this sex bias remains unclear. One hypothesis is that this sex bias is due to genetic variants in X chromosome genes where haploinsufficiency causes neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). In heterozygous XX female probands, a complete loss-of-function variant in one of these genes often causes syndromic NDD, but the same variant is too deleterious for survival in hemizygous XY males. A mild hypomorphic variant, however, may be tolerated in a female carrier but may produce milder neurological phenotypes in a male proband. We tested this by investigating cis-regulatory elements (CREs) of MECP2, a dosage-sensitive gene on the X chromosome where total loss-of-function variants cause Rett syndrome in female children and severe, usually fatal neonatal encephalopathies in male infants. Using a massively parallel reporter assay in human neurons, we mapped transcription factor binding sites within MECP2 CREs and tested autism-associated variants for functional impact. We identified two noncoding variants that change CRE activity and are associated with male-biased autism phenotypes in the proband pedigrees. One of these, a promoter variant, disrupts NFY binding and reduces MECP2 expression by ∼30%, a magnitude that produces social deficits, hyperactivity, and anxiety-like phenotypes in mice. These findings suggest noncoding MECP2 variants can cause idiopathic, male-biased autism and provide a framework for uncovering regulatory variants in other X chromosome neurodevelopmental genes that may contribute to autism's missing heritability.

titulo: The genetic orchestra of autism and its intersections with epilepsy, intellectual disability, and ADHD
resumo: Autism is a complex condition with marked phenotypic variability and a multifactorial etiology orchestrated by diverse genetic and environmental influences. In this review, we dissect what we refer to as autism's "genetic orchestra", spanning from the high-impact "soloists", de novo and ultra-rare variants with large effect sizes, to the "polyphonic background" of common variants which individually exert modest effects but collectively have significant impact. We examine how this orchestra wires neural circuits, with convergent biological pathways modulating synaptic function and chromatin remodeling. Although de novo, rare, and common variants are often studied independently, converging evidence supports a model whereby their influences are largely additive. This genetic orchestra is not condition-specific; autism frequently co-occurs with other neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions, reflecting substantial pleiotropy across both rare and common variant landscapes. Notably, ultra-rare variants tend to associate with co-occurring intellectual disability, ADHD, epilepsy, and psychiatric conditions highlighting their high phenotypic impact. Beyond genetics, layers of environmental and contextual factors further modulate clinical outcomes. In this framework, we also discuss the challenges of identifying genetic variants associated with autism through clinical genetic testing, where yields remain context-dependent, varying by sex and co-occurring conditions. Finally, we address current limitations and future directions in refining our understanding of autism's genetic basis.

titulo: Longitudinal links between prenatal maternal depression and anxiety symptoms and infant temperament: The roles of postnatal symptoms and perceived partner support
periodico: Infant Mental Health Journal: Infancy and Early Childhood
resumo: The perinatal period is marked by heightened vulnerability to maternal depression and anxiety symptoms, which have been associated with early child socio‐emotional development, including difficult temperament. This longitudinal study investigated whether prenatal maternal depression and anxiety symptoms predicted infant difficult temperament at 12 months through parallel mediation by postnatal maternal symptoms and perceived partner support. Given emerging evidence on sex differences in the associations between prenatal maternal distress and early socio‐emotional development, exploratory multi‐group analyses by child sex were also conducted. Pregnant individuals were recruited (October 2020–September 2022) for the Resilience and Perinatal Stress during the Pandemic (RESPPA) study in Quebec, Canada. Measures included the EPDS, GAD‐7, ICQ, and perceived partner support assessed via self‐reported online questionnaires. Path analyses ( N = 1422) were conducted using data from the third pregnancy trimester (T1), three months postpartum (T2), and 12 months postpartum (T3). Separate models were estimated for depression and anxiety symptoms. Greater prenatal depression symptoms predicted higher infant difficult temperament scores, with postnatal depression symptoms and perceived partner support fully mediating this association. Similar findings emerged for anxiety. No significant sex differences were observed. Findings highlight postnatal maternal depression and anxiety symptoms and perceived partner support as potential screening and intervention targets to promote infant development.

titulo: Irritability in the Mix: An Exploratory Study of the Role of Irritability in Characterising Mood Disorders
resumo: Objectives To examine the relationship between irritability and mixed states in bipolar disorder to determine how subjective irritability and mixed symptoms of mania and depression manifest in patients with bipolar disorder over a period of 18 months. Methods This exploratory analysis examined longitudinal data from a randomised controlled trial of a psychological intervention for patients with bipolar disorder. Scores of subjective irritability and mood morbidity were analysed from data sampled over ten timepoints over the trial from 82 patients. Results Significant associations were found between the presence of irritability and mixed symptoms ( F (1, 684) = 20.468, p < 0.001). This relationship remained significant throughout the duration of the study and the administration of a psychological treatment which reduced both ratings of mood and irritability. Notably, when mixed symptoms are absent, irritability nevertheless remained for nearly half the time. Conclusions Irritability and mixed symptoms are phenomenologically linked. The persistence of this link, regardless of the existence of mixed symptoms, suggests that irritability permeates bipolar disorder and is core to its phenomenology. Future studies should interrogate the tethering of mixed symptoms and irritability in the context of bipolar disorder as this may lead to a deeper understanding of the core characteristics of the illness—both clinically and in terms of its neurobiology.

titulo: Loneliness and problematic use of conversational artificial intelligence among college students: the serial mediating roles of social anxiety and self-control
resumo: Objectives Loneliness is an important public health concern associated with individuals’ physical and mental wellbeing. As conversational artificial intelligence (CAI) becomes more widely used, concerns about its problematic use have attracted increasing attention. However, the link between loneliness and problematic use of conversational artificial intelligence (PUCAI) remains insufficiently understood. The current research explored the link between loneliness and PUCAI among college students, with social anxiety and self-control evaluated as serial mediators. These findings provide preliminary empirical insight into the psychological correlates of PUCAI and may inform future research and educational efforts aimed at promoting healthy and responsible CAI use. Methods Using convenience sampling, this cross-sectional study analyzed data from 400 undergraduate students enrolled at a university in western China. Research instruments included the Loneliness Scale, the PUCAI Scale, the Social Anxiety Scale, and the Self-Control Scale. Descriptive statistics and Pearson correlations were computed with IBM SPSS Statistics 26.0. Serial mediation was examined with Hayes’ PROCESS macro (Model 6), and indirect effects were evaluated using 5,000 bootstrap resamples with 95% confidence intervals. Results Greater loneliness was linked to higher PUCAI. Social anxiety and self-control each showed significant indirect associations, and the proposed statistical model indicated a significant serial indirect effect involving these two variables. Conclusion The results offer further insight into the potential psychological pathways associated with PUCAI among college students. The findings suggest that loneliness, social anxiety, and self-regulatory capacities may represent potentially relevant factors to consider in future research and prevention efforts aimed at promoting healthy and responsible CAI use.
palavras_chave: Problematic Use Of Conversational Artificial Intelligence

titulo: Associations of traditional social support and dazi socializing with social anxiety in medical students: the mediating role of psychological resilience
resumo: Objective This study investigated associations of traditional social support (family and friend support) and dazi socializing with social anxiety among medical students, and examined the mediating role of psychological resilience, addressing gaps in integrating the stress-buffering model and conservation of resources theory. Methods Convenience sampling was used to recruit undergraduate students majoring in clinical medicine from the first to fifth years at a university in Zhejiang Province. Participants completed online questionnaires including the Self-developed Questionnaire on Experiences of dazi Socializing, Chinese Version of the Perceived Social Support Scale, Interaction Anxiousness Scale and the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale. Data cleaning and statistical analyses were performed using Python 3.11. ANCOVA was conducted to control for gender, academic year, and student leadership. The mediating effect of psychological resilience was examined using model 4 of Hayes's PROCESS macro and Bootstrap method based on 5,000 resampling iterations. Pearson correlation, hierarchical regression, and independent-samples t tests were applied for intra-group analyses among participants with dazi experiences. Results After controlling for covariates, the dazi group scored higher than non- dazi users in friend support ( F (1,677) = 27.18, p < 0.001), family support ( F (1,677) = 8.45, p = 0.004), and psychological resilience ( F (1,677) = 18.80, p < 0.001). Meanwhile, the dazi group reported lower social anxiety than non- dazi users ( F (1,677) = 22.23, p < 0.001). Mediation analysis showed that psychological resilience fully mediated friend support (indirect effect = −0.0211, 95% CI [−0.0433, −0.0021], 23.4%) and family support (indirect effect = −0.0159, 95% CI [−0.0340, −0.0017], 33.1%) on social anxiety. It partially mediated dazi socializing (direct effect = −1.2215, 95% CI [−1.8773, −0.5439]; indirect effect = −0.0812, 95% CI [−0.1951, −0.0033], 6.2%). Within the dazi group, higher social anxiety was indirectly associated with greater “Safety/Trust concerns”; emotional dazi scored lower on resilience than functional dazi , with the difference approaching significance ( t = −1.94, p = 0.054). Conclusion Both traditional social support and dazi experiences are associated with social anxiety levels among medical students. The relationship between traditional social support and social anxiety is entirely indirect through psychological resilience, whereas the association between dazi experiences and social anxiety is achieved through both direct and indirect pathways via psychological resilience.

titulo: Associations between green space exposure and climate anxiety among Chinese university students: the role of school-based and leisure-time physical activity, nature connectedness, and perceived stress
resumo: Background Climate anxiety has become an important mental health concern among young adults, yet the pathways linking green space exposure to climate-related distress remain unclear. This study examined whether objective green space exposure was associated with climate anxiety among Chinese university students through domain-specific physical activity, nature connectedness, and perceived stress. Methods A cross-sectional study included 918 undergraduate students from four universities in Wuhan Province, China. Residential and campus greenness were assessed using the satellite-derived Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). Moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) was objectively measured using accelerometers and classified as school-based or leisure-time MVPA. Nature connectedness, perceived stress, and climate anxiety were assessed using validated questionnaires. Structural equation modeling with bias-corrected bootstrapping (5,000 resamples) was used to estimate direct and indirect associations while adjusting for relevant covariates. Results Residential greenness was positively associated with leisure-time MVPA and nature connectedness, whereas campus greenness was more strongly associated with school-based MVPA. No significant direct association was observed between residential greenness and climate anxiety after accounting for mediators. However, an inverse indirect association was identified through leisure-time MVPA, nature connectedness, and perceived stress. Leisure-time MVPA showed stronger associations with climate anxiety than school-based MVPA. Nature connectedness displayed a positive direct association with climate anxiety but an inverse indirect association through lower perceived stress. Perceived stress showed the strongest association with climate anxiety. Conclusion These findings suggest that green space may be linked to climate anxiety primarily through behavioral and psychological pathways.

titulo: Factors Influencing the Prevalence of PTSD Tendencies on Social Media During Emergencies
resumo: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a psychological condition that may develop after exposure to severe traumatic events, particularly in unexpected situations characterized by high uncertainty and stress. As social media has become an integral part of daily life, it serves as a platform for sharing personal experiences, emotional expressions, and public responses during emergencies. Grounded in Protection Motivation Theory, this study explores the factors associated with PTSD tendencies expressed on social media during emergencies. Using large-scale user-generated data from social media, posts exhibiting PTSD tendencies were identified through a machine-learning classifier based on semantic embeddings, and the Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic model was applied to extract relevant themes. A multiple linear regression model with Newey–West standard errors was then constructed to examine the factors related to the prevalence of PTSD tendencies. The results indicate that epidemic containment, protective measures, and health concern are negatively associated with the prevalence of PTSD tendencies on social media, whereas expressive negativity is positively associated with trauma-related expression. Focusing on the context of COVID-19, this study highlights the factors associated with PTSD tendencies on social media and underscores the importance of well-organized epidemic prevention and control measures and balanced information dissemination in mitigating the psychological impact during emergencies.

titulo: Gender as a moderating variable in the relationship between childhood traumatic experiences and guilt in adolescents
resumo: Childhood traumatic experiences are associated with the development of self-conscious emotions such as guilt during adolescence; however, the role of gender in this relationship remains insufficiently understood, particularly in Latin American contexts. This study aimed to examine whether gender moderates the relationship between childhood traumatic experiences and guilt in adolescents in Trujillo, Peru. A cross-sectional design was employed with a non-probabilistic sample of adolescents ( N = 200). Childhood trauma was assessed using the Child and Adolescent Trauma Screen, and guilt was measured using the Guilt and Shame Experience Scale (GSES). Moderation analysis was conducted to examine the interaction between trauma and gender. The results indicated that childhood traumatic experiences were significantly associated with guilt. Gender also showed a significant effect and moderated this relationship. Specifically, the association between trauma and guilt was significant among male adolescents but not among females, indicating gender-based differences in trauma-related emotional processing. These findings highlight the relevance of gender in understanding the relationship between childhood trauma and guilt during adolescence. The study provides evidence from a Latin American context and underscores the need for gender-sensitive approaches in the assessment and intervention of trauma-related emotional outcomes, supporting the development of targeted prevention and intervention strategies aimed at reducing psychological distress in adolescents.

titulo: Family and Domestic Violence Discretion and Decision-Making Through the Perspectives of Social Workers and Victim-Survivors
resumo: Social workers (SWs) employed in family and domestic violence (FDV) roles use their discretion and make decisions that impact victim-survivor (VS) outcomes and well-being. However, when working alongside VSs, discretion and decision-making remain unexplored in existing literature. This study examined social work discretion and decision-making in FDV contexts and its impacts on VSs. Interpretative phenomenological analysis underpinned eight semistructured interviews with SWs and VSs to explore experiences of discretion and decision-making within FDV contexts. The findings suggest a lack of discretion steers SWs down a standardized path of risk-averse practice, which works against VS needs.

titulo: Virtual Reality–Assisted Therapy Compared to Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Patients With Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenia: Assessor-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial
resumo: Background Auditory verbal hallucinations (AVH) are among the most disabling symptoms of schizophrenia and often persist despite treatment. Virtual reality–assisted therapies (VRTs) are a new generation of relational interventions for AVH, but comparative evidence against active interventions is currently lacking. Objective This study aimed to assess whether VRT (9 sessions) is superior to a short course of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) targeting AVH (9 sessions) in reducing AVH in individuals with treatment-resistant schizophrenia. Methods In this assessor-blind, parallel-group randomized controlled trial conducted from 2019 to 2026 at an academic center in Montreal (Canada), adults with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder and persistent AVH were either referred by their health care team or self-referred. A total of 136 participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to VRT or CBT, stratified by sex and clozapine use status. Both 9-session interventions targeted maladaptive beliefs and relationships with voices and were administered by trained psychotherapists. The predetermined primary outcome was the evolution of AVH severity over time, measured at baseline, post treatment, and 3 months post therapy using the auditory hallucination subscale of the Psychotic Symptoms Rating Scale. Secondary outcomes notably included the general psychotic symptomatology measured using the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess time-by-treatment interactions. Psychotherapy sessions and assessments were conducted primarily in person, with CBT being occasionally delivered via videoconferencing during the COVID-19 pandemic. Results Participants had a mean age of 40.3 (SD 12.8) years, 63.2% (86/136) were male, and 56.6% (77/136) received clozapine. Intention-to-treat analyses (VRT, n=67; CBT, n=69) showed a significant time-by-treatment interaction favoring VRT ( P =.013) with a moderate effect size at 3 months post therapy (Cohen d =0.614). Both therapies showed significant within-group improvements in the primary outcome, with large effect sizes for VRT (Cohen d =0.81 post therapy and Cohen d =1.17 at 3 months) and moderate for CBT (Cohen d =0.58 post therapy and Cohen d =0.39 at 3 months). While there were no between-group differences for secondary outcomes, within-group improvements were observed in psychotic symptoms, emotional regulation, and voice acceptance for both therapies, and VRT also reduced maladaptive beliefs about voices and improved self-esteem. Conclusions VRT outperformed a targeted short course of CBT in reducing persistent AVH for up to 3 months after the intervention in a North American population with treatment-resistant schizophrenia. Improvements were also seen in some secondary outcomes, such as general psychotic symptomatology, and those were similar for both interventions. Overall, these findings support the value of VRT as a personalized and clinically effective intervention.

titulo: Which Theoretical Models or Frameworks Are Used to Understand Trauma‐Informed Care in Mental Health Settings? A Scoping Review
periodico: International Journal of Mental Health Nursing
resumo: This scoping review examines and synthesizes the theoretical foundations underpinning trauma‐informed care (TIC) in mental health settings. A systematic search of CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed yielded 1278 records, of which 23 peer‐reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2025 met the inclusion criteria. Reporting followed the PRISMA‐ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta‐Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) checklist and explanation. Seven overarching theoretical domains were identified: neurobiological and psychophysiological foundations, psychological and relational models, adverse childhood experiences and social determinants frameworks, SAMHSA and Harris & Fallot principles, socio‐ecological and intersectional frameworks, organizational and implementation science models, and integrated or hybrid approaches. These frameworks highlight the multidimensional nature of trauma and its implications for mental health nursing practice, interdisciplinary care, organizational change, and policy development. The findings underscore that TIC is not a single model but a pluralistic and evolving concept bridging individual, relational, and structural dimensions of trauma. Theoretical clarity can enhance implementation fidelity, reduce re‐traumatization, and support recovery‐oriented care. Future research should focus on evaluating hybrid frameworks and linking theoretical models to measurable individual, organizational, and system‐level outcomes.

titulo: Prevention and mitigation strategies for psychological disorders in European ongoing and post-war settings: lessons from the 2022 Russo-Ukrainian war
resumo: There is an ongoing need to facilitate the development and implementation of preventative measures and prophylactic steps to mitigate the development of psychiatric disorders such as posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) within traumatized populations in theaters of war (e.g., 2022 Russo-Ukrainian War). If successful, these measures have the potential to reduce the incidence, severity, and duration of psychological distress and posttraumatic stress reactions, including PTSD, while increasing the likelihood of resilience. This conceptual analysis paper will review the psychological effects of either living in, or being displaced from, active war zones in Europe. The ongoing situation in Ukraine will be used as an example, with specific emphasis on risk and resilience factors, prevention strategies spanning therapeutic domains, and how we can apply what the medical and scientific communities have learned in the aftermath of other global armed conflicts historically. As such, the paper will close with a discussion of the empirically recommended mental health interventions and tools that should be made available to the non-displaced Ukrainian population, internally and external displaced individuals (refugees), as well as citizens of host countries that receive refugee populations.

titulo: Mental Health of First Responders in Rural Australia: A Qualitative Exploration of Intersecting Individual, Organisational and Contextual Factors on Psychological Wellbeing
periodico: International Journal of Mental Health Nursing
resumo: To explore the factors shaping mental health experiences among rural and remote first responders and to examine how organisational and contextual conditions influence psychological wellbeing. First responders are routinely exposed to traumatic events and are at elevated risk of mental health difficulties. In rural and remote settings, geographic isolation, limited workforce capacity, and reduced access to specialised services may compound these risks. However, less is known about how workplace culture and service structures interact with trauma exposure in these contexts. A participatory action research (PAR) approach was used to co‐design this study, using phenomenological qualitative methods through semi‐structured interviews with rural and remote first responders. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis informed by phenomenological principles to explore lived experience. An advisory group contributed to the interpretation and refinement of findings. Participants described cumulative mental health strain arising not only from trauma exposure but also from structural and cultural conditions embedded within rural service environments. Geographic isolation, small team structures, high workload, and limited anonymity intensified emotional labour. Workplace cultures characterised by expectations of stoicism, ‘hero’ narratives, misogyny and gender discrimination, and limited recognition contributed to moral distress and psychological burden. Participants identified significant gaps in mental health service provision, including limited access to trauma‐informed and first responder‐specific supports in rural areas. Mental health challenges among rural first responders are shaped by intersecting individual, organisational, and structural factors. Trauma exposure alone does not account for the complexity of distress experienced in these settings. Interventions must extend beyond individual resilience‐building to include organisational reform, psychologically safe workplace cultures, and improved access to tailored, trauma‐informed mental health services in rural and remote contexts.

titulo: Transformational Clinical Matrix-Expanded: Metatheoretical Framework for Conceptualizing Dysfunctional Processes and Psychopathology
resumo: Complex psychopathology, particularly when associated with adverse developmental experiences and complex trauma, involves multiple cognitive, affective, behavioral, interpersonal, and neurobiological processes that may be difficult to organize within single-theoretical or symptom-based models. The present paper introduces the Transformational Clinical Matrix-Expanded (TCM-XP), a transdiagnostic and metatheoretical framework developed to organize these processes within a developmental and integrative perspective. The TCM-XP comprises seven interrelated domains: Adverse and Dysfunctional Experiences, Emotional Wounds, Dialectical Core Schemas, Affective Dysregulation, Coping and Dispositional Responses, Maladaptive Patterns, and Complex Neural Network Dysfunctions. These domains are proposed to operate recursively rather than independently, suggesting that adverse relational and contextual experiences may contribute to the frustration of core biopsychosocial pressures, affectively encoded emotional wounds, polarized cognitive-affective representations, affective dysregulation, and recurrent coping and interpersonal patterns. The model also considers the possible contribution of large-scale brain networks and related neurobiological systems without reducing psychological functioning to neural mechanisms. By integrating developmental psychopathology, trauma theory, clinical psychology, personality perspectives, and affective neuroscience, TCM-XP provides a conceptual organization of complex psychological functioning that may inform assessment, case conceptualization, and clinical decision-making.

titulo: Predictors and Moderators of Post-Treatment Depression Severity After Hypnotherapy and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy in an RCT for Mild-to-Moderate Depression
resumo: Depression is one of the most prevalent mental health conditions, and cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is one of the most efficacious treatments for depressive disorders. Several studies have demonstrated the efficacy of hypnotherapy (HT) in treating depression. However, it remains unclear which treatment works the best for each patient. This study investigated global and treatment-specific predictors of CBT and HT in a secondary analysis of an RCT for patients with mild-to-moderate major depression. A total of 152 patients were randomly assigned to receive either HT (n = 74) or CBT (n = 78) as an individual outpatient treatment for six months. Both treatments were comparably effective. Baseline characteristics including sociodemographic, depression-related, and psychological variables were assessed. The primary outcome was the clinician-rated Montgomery–Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) scores after the treatment. Predictors were examined using correlation, regression, and moderation analyses for hypothesis-generating purposes. The results did not support the hypothesized cognitive and behavioral variables predicting post-treatment depression severity for CBT nor hypnotic susceptibility or expectations predicting outcome for HT. We found that lower baseline depression severity and higher self-efficacy predicted a better overall treatment outcome for all patients. As exploratory results, antidepressant medication and environmental quality of life predicted treatment outcome for patients receiving HT. In patients with CBT, educational level and psychological quality of life were found as exploratory predictors of treatment outcome. These results should be considered preliminary before strong conclusions can be drawn. Future research should further investigate HT and refine predictor models more strictly.

titulo: Patient-reported outcome measures within European cohorts of severely injured patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
periodico: European Journal of Trauma and Emergency Surgery
resumo: Purpose Severe injury affects multiple health-related domains, yet comprehensive European data on patient-reported outcomes remain limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) use and outcomes in severely injured European cohorts. Methods A systematic search of four databases up to October 14, 2025, identified European studies from 2000 onward reporting PROMs in severely injured patients. Severe injury was defined as an Injury Severity Score ≥ 16, Glasgow Coma Scale ≤ 8, intensive care unit admission, spinal cord injury, traumatic amputations, or pelvic fractures. Two reviewers independently screened records, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Meta-analysis was performed when ≥ 3 studies reported comparable PROMs at similar follow-up timepoints. Results Of 2,479 studies, 119 were included. Most cohorts originated from the Netherlands (26%), Norway (18%), and Germany (16%). General severely injured cohorts were most frequently studied (61%), followed by traumatic brain injury (17%), and spinal cord injury (15%). In total, 94 PROMs were used across 277 follow-up timepoints. Health-related quality of life was assessed most frequently (63%), after that anxiety/depression (14%), post-traumatic stress (9%), and social functioning (6%). At one year follow-up, the pooled EuroQol-5D-3 L index score was 0.70 ( 95% CI 0.62–0.77) and VAS score was 68 ( 95% CI 60–75), indicating persistent impairment compared to population norms. Conclusion Severely injured patients show persistent impairments with incomplete restoration of pre-injury functioning. Despite increased PROMs use, heterogeneity in selection and outcome reporting limits comparability, underscoring the need for standardised PROM assessment to improve outcome evaluation after severe injury.

titulo: Canvas of Strength: A Mixed-Methods Pilot Study of a Community-Based Arts Intervention for Women Survivors of Domestic Violence in China
resumo: Women survivors of domestic violence often experience persistent psychological distress, yet evidence supporting community-based arts interventions remains limited, particularly in mainland China. This mixed-methods pilot study evaluated the preliminary effectiveness of Canvas of Strength, a community-based arts intervention for women survivors of domestic violence in Liaoning Province, China. Sixteen participants were recruited from a community service center and allocated to intervention (n = 8) and control (n = 8) groups. Depression, anxiety, and self-esteem were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and six-month follow-up using standardized measures, while semi-structured interviews explored participants’ experiences. The intervention group demonstrated significant improvements across all three psychological outcomes following the intervention, with these gains largely maintained at six-month follow-up, whereas no significant changes were observed in the control group. Qualitative findings revealed enhanced emotional expression, positive cognitive reframing, improved self-perception, and strengthened interpersonal and social engagement, providing contextual support for the quantitative findings. Together, these findings suggest that Canvas of Strength shows promise as a community-based arts intervention for improving the psychological well-being of women survivors of domestic violence. Given the pilot nature and small sample size of this study, further evaluation in adequately powered trials is warranted.

titulo: Understanding and applying psychological formulation in secure children's homes: Insights from residential staff
periodico: Psychology and Psychotherapy: Theory, Research and Practice
resumo: Objectives Psychological formulation helps to develop an understanding of an individual's experiences and how they make sense of these. There is limited research around staff's perspectives of psychological formulation within the Children and Young People Secure Estate (CYPSE). The aim of this research was to explore residential staff's lived experiences of utilising and applying formulation into their practice, discover the impact on working relationships with young people (YP) and identify what role formulation has for future practice and policy. Design and Methods Nine qualitative semi‐structured interviews were facilitated with residential staff in two secure children's homes (SCH) in England. An interpretative phenomenological analysis approach was utilised, and five themes were developed. Results Psychological formulation enhanced trauma‐informed understandings, promoted collaboration among professionals, helped to develop therapeutic relationships with YP, created psychological safety and promoted empowerment. Additionally, formulation processes were flexible, which helped staff to adapt their approaches to be more trauma‐informed and person‐centred. Conclusions Future practice/policy should consider systemic challenges limiting engagement and prioritise YP's views on being involved in the formulation process. Implications for clinical practice are discussed as well as recommendations for future research.
palavras_chave: Children And Young Person Secure Estate

titulo: The overlap of child abuse, neglect, and exposure to domestic violence in court-involved children with a history of maltreatment: Frequency and correlates
resumo: Background Child maltreatment--including child abuse and neglect (CAN) and exposure to domestic violence (EDV)--is a pervasive international issue. Although research on maltreatment is extensive, studies of co-occurring CAN and EDV among court-involved samples are limited. Objective Among a court-involved sample of maltreated children referred for expert psychological assessment, this study examined (1) the frequency of CAN and EDV, (2) the co-occurrence of maltreatment subtypes (including EDV), and (3) risk factors associated with co-occurring CAN and EDV. Participants and setting We conducted a retrospective examination of case records for 279 Australian children (child age M = 7.96 years, SD = 4.25 years) within 151 families referred for psychological assessment due to maltreatment-related child protective concerns by the Children's Court of Victoria. Methods Descriptive analyses assessed the frequency and co-occurrence of maltreatment subtypes. Binary logistic regression models examined child, parent, and family-level risk factors associated with co-occurring CAN and EDV. Results Nearly two-thirds (63.44%) of children experienced both CAN and EDV. Over three quarters (77.42%; n = 216) experienced two or more of the five types of maltreatment. The most common combination was EDV with neglect (20.07%, n = 52). Significant risk factors associated with the co-occurrence of CAN and EDV included child (serious behaviour problems), parent (substance use), and family-level (serious family and socioeconomic stress, lack of social support) variables. Conclusions Findings demonstrate the high co-occurrence of CAN and EDV, and their complex risk profile, among court-involved families with these experiences. Implications, including the prioritization of children and families for support and intervention, are discussed.

titulo: Comparative Effects of Various Delivery Methods of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia Among Patients With Cancers: Systematic Review and Network Meta‐Analysis
resumo: Background Insomnia affects 30%–60% of cancer survivors, with around 20% meeting criteria for insomnia disorder. Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBTi) is the first‐line treatment, but access is limited by cost and therapist availability, prompting exploration of alternative delivery modes, including digital interventions. Purpose To systematically review and conduct a network meta‐analysis (NMA) of the efficacy of different CBTi delivery methods for managing insomnia in cancer survivors. Methods The PubMed, Embase, CINAHL and Cochrane Library were searched for relevant articles published before September 25, 2025. Only randomized controlled trials of adult cancer patients evaluating the effects of any CBTi delivery mode on subjective sleep outcomes were included. Primary outcome was insomnia severity index (ISI) score; secondary outcomes included sleep onset latency (SOL), wake after sleep onset (WASO), total sleep time (TST), and sleep efficiency (SE). A frequentist random‐effects NMA was conducted. Results Twenty‐two trials involving 2040 participants were included. Compared with treatment as usual (TAU), digital CBTi (dCBTi) demonstrated the largest reduction in ISI scores (MD = −9.70, 95% CI = −10.80 to −8.61), followed by telephone CBTi (MD = −8.74). dCBTi also significantly improved SOL (−30.95 min), WASO (−25.62 min), TST (+31.67 min), and SE (+14.63%). Group CBTi significantly improved SOL (−11.60 min) and WASO (−22.03 min). Meta‐regression analyses identified breast cancer diagnosis as a significant moderator of dCBTi effects on SOL (coefficient = 25.20, p = 0.015) and SE (coefficient = −16.17, p = 0.007). The certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low, primarily because of imprecision and network incoherence. Conclusions dCBTi demonstrated the greatest potential for improving insomnia outcomes among the evaluated CBTi delivery modalities. However, given the low certainty of evidence and the presence of network inconsistency for selected outcomes, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. High‐quality head‐to‐head trials are needed to confirm the comparative effectiveness of different CBTi delivery modalities in oncology populations. Trial Registration The study protocol was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (registration no. CRD42023429081)

titulo: Exploring the Forms and Risk Factors of Domestic Violence from Afghan Immigrant Women’s Point of View in Finland
resumo: Migration, particularly forced migration, often heightens vulnerability to domestic violence (DV) due to a complex interplay of cultural, structural, and migration-related stressors. While Finland is recognized for its high standards of gender equality, it also reports high rates of domestic violence against women (DVAW), with a gap in research focusing specifically on the perceptions of Afghan immigrant women. To address this gap, this qualitative study investigates how Afghan immigrant women in Finland conceptualize DV and identify its underlying drivers. Utilizing a transnational intersectional framework, the research examines how multiple, overlapping identities, such as ethnicity, religion, and migration status, shape understandings of violence across borders. Methodologically, the study adopts a qualitative approach, conducting semi-structured interviews with 13 Afghan women residing in Finland to explore their understandings of DVAW and its associated risk factors. The findings reveal a multilayered understanding of violence that extends beyond the individual to familial and communal levels. Key themes include physical and emotional violence, characterized by physical assault, blaming women, and neglect. Economic abuse and coercive control were manifested through denied financial autonomy, interference of in-law families, and forced marriage. Sexual violence was defined by the unimportance of women’s desires and a lack of discretion in matters related to pregnancy. Risk factors were attributed to individual and family factors, such as women’s behavior and the influence of men and family, as well as communal and societal factors, including culture, community, religion, and the psychological legacy of war. The study highlights a gap in violence-preventing social work, showing that a “fear of the system” often prevents women from seeking help and accessing support service. To address these barriers, the research suggests that integration policies and social work practices must evolve from purely interventionist models to culturally sensitive, trust-based approaches that prioritize the dissemination of rights-based information in native languages and engage community leaders in prevention efforts.

titulo: Exploring the impact of teacher expectations on student behavior and academic performance using cognitive behavioral therapy
resumo: This study evaluated the effectiveness of using a cognitive-behavioral therapy based teacher training program to change teachers’ expectations of students and improve student behavior and academic performance. This paper designs and uses a quasi experimental approach with a non equivalent control group for pre-test/post test. The participants consist of 115 third grade teachers and 356 third grade students from five primary schools. Teachers identified as having low expectations received a 12 week manual CBT training program, while those identified as having high expectations were used as the control group. This study used the Teacher Expectations Scale to measure teacher expectations, the Student Behavior Observation Scale to measure changes in student behavior, and standardized Chinese and math tests to measure improvements in student academic performance. The results showed that after implementing the intervention, the teacher’s expected score significantly increased from the baseline original ratio to a higher score (after the intervention) through statistical analysis ( t = 4.15, p < 0.001; Cohen’s d = 0.72). In addition, the number of students who scored over 80 points in academic tests increased during the five testing processes (40.40% in the pre-test and 76.20% in the post test); also, compared with baseline measurements, the positive behavior rate of students taught by teachers who received intervention increased, while the negative behavior rate decreased.

titulo: Cumulative Exposure to Harsh Discipline at Home and School on Child Development: Evidence From Ghana
resumo: Violence against children violates human rights and fundamentally challenges the global objectives outlined in the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Children may frequently experience harsh discipline in both homes and schools, two main settings for early learning and development, yet longitudinal evidence on the developmental consequences of exposure to harsh discipline across these two settings remains scarce in Sub‐Saharan Africa. Further, the interaction between harsh discipline at home and in school remains underexplored. Drawing on data from a longitudinal study in Ghana, we examine whether repeated exposure to harsh discipline at home and school across three years (which we define as “cumulative exposure”) among pre‐primary school children aged 5–8 years ( N = 663; M age = 6.94 years). By controlling for baseline outcomes in a value‐added design, we estimated the robust associations between cumulative harsh discipline at home and at schools with higher‐order cognitive skills, namely academic and executive function. Cumulative harsh discipline at home significantly predicted lower academic skills (𝛽 = ‐0.045, p < 0.05) but not executive function, while cumulative harsh discipline at school did not statistically significantly predict any skills. Moderation analyses showed that children's experiences of harsh discipline at home were negatively associated with executive function under conditions of low levels of harsh discipline at school. Findings highlight the urgent need for integrated, contextually grounded interventions targeting home and school disciplinary practices to support early learning and development in Sub‐Saharan Africa.

titulo: Domestic violence and mental health: Legal issues in clinical practice
resumo: Background Healthcare is a heavily regulated environment in which nurses must navigate the delivery of therapeutic care while also managing their legal responsibilities. Appropriate care may appear ambiguous when the person who has experienced domestic or family violence is also experiencing mental health issues. Aim This study aims to present a case study, with learning objectives aligned to core legal, ethical, and clinical decision-making considerations and then demonstrate how students can be guided to analyse the case study, identify legal concerns, and address the arising issues to provide appropriate mental healthcare. Research Design A simulated, constructed teaching case was analysed against relevant Australian legislation, professional standards, and organizational policy to identify key legal and practice issues at the intersection of domestic and family violence and mental healthcare. Ethical Considerations Simulated case studies include realistic details that mirror practice environments. This case, designed for educational purposes, does not reproduce or disclose any real patient information, thereby avoiding confidentiality and ethical concerns. Results Recommendations surrounding lawful information sharing and the use of least-restrictive practices have been made. There is a need to support nurses with relevant education aligned with clear policies that reflect legislation. Conclusions This article highlights how legislation underpins and influences the provision of safe trauma-informed healthcare. Where domestic and family violence intersect with mental deterioration nursing staff need to navigate between their legal and ethical role and responsibilities. Using a simulated case study this article provides recommendations for care for these often-complex presentations.

titulo: United States, British, and New Zealand Broadsheet Representations of Domestic Violence Before and After the Onset of the COVID-19 Pandemic
